verdict.rationale: uv's own docs state it is 'Disk-space efficient, with a global cache for dependency deduplication' and that it caches aggressively to avoid re-downloading dependencies, which is direct but thin support for a shared store. A community report of moving to uv when pip's cache was eating disk space on a quota-limited server adds mild corroboration. One user's report that uvx sometimes re-downloads dependencies is anecdotal and does not concretely contradict on-disk deduplication. missing for 10: documentation that the store is content-addressable, evidence that projects link to (rather than copy) the cached packages so each version exists once on disk, and an in-depth cache-design reference beyond a one-line feature claim.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on a shared content-addressable store so the same dependency version is stored once on disk across all projects

citations.quote: Disk-space efficient, with a global cache for dependency deduplication.
uv uses aggressive caching to avoid re-downloading (and re-building) dependencies that have already been accessed in prior runs.
